content.title: Meet the New Characters Joining 'The Pitt' Season 2 (Including Dr. Robby's Replacement!)
content.text: 'The Pitt' season 2 introduces several new characters joining the team at Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center Published on January 8, 2026 08:00AM EST Gerran Howell, Amielynn Abellera, Noah Wyle, Sepideh Moafi and Supriya Ganesh in The Pitt. Credit : Warrick Page/MAX NEED TO KNOW The Pitt is returning for season 2 on Jan. 8The Emmy Award-winning series will star several returning characters — such as Noah Wyle's Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch — as well as new starsSome of the new cast members include Sepideh Moafi, Meta Golding, Luke Tennie and Christopher Thornton The Pitt is gearing up for another intense season. The Emmy Award-winning medical procedural tells the story of doctors and nurses operating in the fictional Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center over the course of a typical hours-long shift. For season 2 of The Pitt, which premieres Jan. 8 on HBO Max, the characters will deal with incoming patients over Fourth of July weekend. Similar to the first season, season 2 will feature returning stars Noah Wyle — who also served as an executive producer — as Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch, Patrick Ball as Dr. Frank Langdon, Katherine LaNasa as Dana Evans, Supriya Ganesh as Dr. Samira Mohan, Fiona Dourif as Dr. Cassie McKay, Taylor Dearden as Dr. Melissa "Mel" King, Isa Briones as Dr. Trinity Santos, Gerran Howell as Dennis Whitaker and Shabana Azeez as Victoria Javadi. Prior to season 2, Tracy Ifeachor — who played Dr. Heather Collins — announced that she'd be leaving the show for creative reasons but still expressed gratitude for being part of the "groundbreaking" series. In addition to the returning stars, season 2 will also introduce several new characters. Sepideh Moafi will join the main cast as Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi, a new attending physician who's been sent to replace Dr. Robby when he goes on a planned sabbatical. Meanwhile, Meta Golding, Luke Tennie and Christopher Thornton all scored recurring roles. Here's everything to know about The Pitt season 2 new characters. Sepideh Moafi as Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi Sepideh Moafi in The Pitt. Warrick Page/MAX Moafi is joining The Pitt season 2 cast as Dr. Robby's potential replacement, Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi. As Dr. Robby is preparing to leave the Pitt for a three-month sabbatical, he gets to know the new woman in charge. Dr. Al-Hashimi comes to the hospital from the VA, where she previously worked with Dr. Mohan and Dr. King. However, Dr. Al-Hashimi and Dr. Robby may not have the smoothest transition, as she's already implementing ideas — including new technology — to "elevate" the efficiency of the hospital. "Robby's innately suspicious of anything that could potentially allow a hospital to reduce its workforce because of the streamlining," Wyle teased to Entertainment Weekly in December 2025. "There are byproducts to employing this kind of technology. One of the unfortunate ones is layoffs, and we're already seeing staffing shortages." However, Moafi said that her character is determined to make her mark and is used to facing "resistance, especially from your male counterparts." "She's ready, she's equipped, she's prepared," the actress told the outlet. "And like most women, and especially women of color, you are over prepared for whatever challenges you might face. And so I don't think it throws her off." Meta Golding as Nurse Noelle Hastings Meta Golding attends the "Rabbit Hole" Premiere on March 12, 2023 in Austin, Texas. Rick Kern/Getty Golding will sport a pair of scrubs as nurse Noelle Hastings in season 2, although her character's background and context have not been shared. The actress expressed her excitement about joining the cast by posting a screenshot announcing her hiring. She captioned the photo, "Some good news to share: yours truly has joined The Pitt on HBO." Luke Tennie as Dr. Crus Henderson Luke Tennie attends the 77th Primetime Emmy Awards Nominees Celebration on September 13, 2025 in Beverly Hills, California. Maya Dehlin Spach/Getty Tennie scored a recurring role as Dr. Henderson, a Pitt fourth year resident on the night shift. After his role was announced, Tennie posted on Instagram that he "loved" The Pitt prior to joining the series. Christopher Thornton as Dr. Caleb Jefferson Christopher Thornton attends the premiere of "History of the World, Part II" on February 27, 2023 in Los Angeles, California. Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Thornton will join The Pitt as Dr. Caleb Jefferson, a psychiatric attending at PTMC. His character is recurring, but he's expected to appear in around seven of the 15 episodes in the second season, per his IMDb. Thornton is known for his role as Kenny "Shammy" Shamberg in Magnum P.I., as well as acting in The Lincoln Lawyer, Rules of Engagement and Vice Principals. When Thornton was 25 years old, in 1992, he was injured in a rock climbing accident that left him paralyzed from the waist down.
